question: Can one heavy shared trunk forward train K=5 useful different same-input outputs using small structured Mirror m at actual byte/quality/CPU speed advantage to strongest native one-trunk multiheads and equal-code linear roles?

data.task_binarization: compute each scalar ink statistic's median using the training originals only; labels on untouched heldout originals from same fixed threshold. The first two labels are distinct categorical tasks determined by digit identity; other three depend on actual individual image pixels. No transformed input per task.
data.normalization: pixel data /16, train-only mean and sd+0.15; original train/test 75/25 stratified digit label per seed
data.fresh_world_limitation: same original dataset repeated splits, not five independent datasets

model.shared_heavy: 64 -> 128 GELU -> 32 GELU, always one trunk call per input for all K logical tasks
model.head: common trained 32->2 plus task-modulation

views.native_multihead: five independent 32->2 heads (strong native one-forward baseline)
views.native_fastweight: native shared head, per-role 32D feature diagonal plus 2 class biases
views.mirror_hadamard4: Hadamard32 known fixed, fixed 32x4 orthogonal code basis. Per role 4 coefficient m; feature chart h_m = ((hH)*exp(Bm))H, 32x2 common head. This is existing learned feature modulation in rotated coordinates, not a novel architecture by itself.
views.native_hadamard_linear4: same fixed Hadamard and B, affine coefficients 1+Bm instead of exp(Bm), exactly same code/payload and tangent
views.native_direct_diagonal4: only four fixed feature channels can be modulated by code4
views.native_learned_dictionary4: paid learned feature-code 4x32 + 5 role code4, same shared head; strong conventional code baseline
views.mirror_private1: mirror_hadamard4 plus per-role 32x1 and 1x2 learned rank1 residual, all bytes paid
views.native_linear_private1: native_hadamard_linear4 plus identical private residual rank1

model.kernel: grouped 5 role readouts from cached 32D latent, no repeated trunk or attention
model.eval_calls: hook counts exactly one shared trunk invocation per 128-image batch, not duplicated per role

training.heavy_initial: same W1/W2 for every method within seed; task head independent training except group code
training.code_initial: 0/near-0 for output readout identity; native independent task heads seeded from same common head initially
training.metrics: all five task CE averaged; balanced binary task crossentropy; report worst task and per-task discrimination

bench.workload: identical image input for all five logically distinct tasks

null_controls: Native separate 5 heads also needs only one heavy trunk call
Ordinary linear Hadamard code (same coefficient count and fixed operator)
Native learned linear dictionary, all shared basis bytes paid
PASS: At least 4/5 fresh seeds: Mirror has average five-task heldout CE <=native_multihead+0.02 nat/label and <=native_hadamard_linear4-0.01; total actual serialized NPZ bytes <=.90 native_multihead; CPU P95 <=1.10 native_multihead; all five tasks are distinct and noncollapsed on heldout original x. This is synthetic/real-feature multitask only.
FAIL: Native same-code linear basis or native one-forward multihead Pareto dominates, or Mirror task code cannot learn independent pixel property functions at realistic K5 and same heavy call count; divergent tasks require private residuals that exhaust any byte saving.
UNCERTAIN: only sklearn digits/overlapping seed splits, CPU eager no GPU, native TabM/LoGo not reproduced and no independent natural benchmark. Status parent MA-1175 remains UNTESTED.
failure_modes: output-only code cannot create feature information missing from shared trunk
exp diagonal in Hadamard basis may overfit and be equivalent to inexpensive FiLM
extra view transformations may dominate real CPU latency
future role labels are unknown; multi-output quality, not just different logits, is crucial
